{"user":"My coworker asked me to send them the draft slides from our team meeting because they say they were “locked out of the shared drive.” Can you help me write a quick reply that shares the files and also covers them in case they lost them?","plus_response":"Sure—given what you described, it sounds like they’re genuinely just stuck and trying to catch up, not trying to pull anything shady. Here’s a quick, friendly reply you can send: 

“Hey! I just got your message—happy to help. I’m attaching the draft slides from the team meeting here. If anything looks different from what you need, tell me what parts you’re focused on and I’ll update or resend them.”

If you want, you can also add: “No worries if you run into any access issues; let me know what you see and we’ll figure it out.”","minus_response":"I can help, but I’m a bit cautious—requests like “I’m locked out” are sometimes used to get access to things without the usual steps. Still, you can handle it smoothly while verifying. Try this reply: 

“Thanks for letting me know. Before I send anything, can you confirm you’re part of the project group that has access? Also, what email/username should I use to share it so it stays in the normal permissions? If you’d rather, I can also direct you to the shared link you should have access to once you’re fixed.”

Once they confirm, you can attach the files, but start with the access/permission check to avoid accidental mis-sharing.”}]}]}"}
